A branch current sensor measures total current upstream of the connector contactors. A controller communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus.

The controller stores, for each active connector, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current, and an energy-deficit value. The controller sends each assigned limit through the control-pilot interface and verifies the resulting connector current with the corresponding current sensor.

The branch current sensor is an independent safety input. If measured branch current remains above the branch limit after a reduced pilot command for a verification interval, the controller opens connector contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order until measured branch current is below the branch limit. A contactor is not reclosed until its connector current sensor reports zero, the control-pilot interface reports a connected vehicle, and a randomized recovery delay has expired. A welded-contactor condition is recorded when connector current remains above a leakage threshold after an open command. The controller then inhibits the other contactors on the same branch and operates a local fault indicator.

The controller can receive remote schedules and authorizations through a network interface, but it stores a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory. During a network outage it continues already authorized sessions subject to the last accepted branch limit and the independent branch-current safety process. It does not start a newly connected session unless the local token authorizes that connector and has not expired. Meter records are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence and uploaded when communication returns.

The association is stored only after the sensed channel agrees with the commanded connector. This prevents a wiring-map error from assigning a current limit to the wrong connector.

Offline authorization, welded-contactor isolation, tamper-evident records, and installation mapping are supported additional features.

content.content:
1	Sites that install several electric-vehicle charging connectors frequently supply those connectors from a single electrical branch. The branch is protected at an allowable aggregate current, referred to herein as a branch limit, that is commonly lower than the sum of the individual connector ratings. Installing a branch large enough for every connector to draw its full rating at the same time is often impractical, because the cost of the additional service capacity, conductors, and protective devices can exceed the cost of the charging equipment itself.
2	
3	Charging equipment therefore has to share a fixed amount of current among connectors that could collectively demand more. The signalling mechanism ordinarily available for that purpose is the control pilot presented to each vehicle, which advertises a maximum current that the vehicle is permitted to draw. Control-pilot signalling is advisory in nature. The value advertised on the pilot is a command, not a measurement, and the current actually drawn depends on the behaviour of the vehicle receiving it. A vehicle may respond slowly, may respond only in coarse steps, may hold a previous value while its own thermal or state-of-charge logic settles, or may not reduce at all. Control that assumes the commanded value is the delivered value therefore has no way to detect the case in which the branch remains loaded above its limit after a reduction has been ordered, and that case is precisely the one in which the branch protective device is at risk of operating and removing service from every connector on the branch.
4	
5	A further difficulty arises because the branch usually carries loads other than charging. Lighting, building services, and other equipment on the same branch consume part of the allowable aggregate current, and that consumption varies through the day. Allocation that divides the full branch limit among the connectors, without accounting for the varying non-charging portion of the branch load, either overcommits the branch or forces the installer to configure a permanently conservative limit that wastes capacity for most of the day.
6	
7	Sharing schemes that divide available current equally, or in proportion to instantaneous request, also tend to treat every session alike. Where sessions have been served unequally over the course of a shared-capacity period, for example because one session began while the branch was heavily loaded and another began while it was lightly loaded, equal division perpetuates the inequality rather than correcting it.
8	
9	Charging equipment is additionally exposed to conditions that are specific to its power path and its installation. A contactor whose contacts have welded continues to pass current after an open command has been issued, so an allocation scheme that treats an open command as removal of the load will continue to believe that capacity has been released when it has not. Site communication to a remote management system is not continuous, so equipment that depends on a remote authority for both authorization and current limits either stops serving vehicles when the link fails or continues without a governing limit. Multi-connector equipment is also wired by hand, and a transposition between the logical identifier of a connector and the physical contactor and sensor channel that serve it causes a current limit intended for one connector to be applied to another, which defeats the allocation entirely while leaving every individual component apparently functional.
10	
11	There remains a need for charging control that treats the current actually present on the branch and at each connector as the governing quantity, that keeps the branch within its limit even when a vehicle does not honour a reduced pilot command, that allocates the genuinely available portion of the branch limit in a way that corrects accumulated inequality between sessions, and that remains safe and operable when the site link is down, when a contactor has welded, and when the installation wiring map has not been independently confirmed.
12

1	In the following description, reference is made to the accompanying drawings, which form a part of this disclosure and show particular embodiments by way of illustration. Other embodiments may be used and structural or logical changes may be made without departing from the scope of the disclosure. Like reference numerals designate like parts throughout the several views.
2	
3	Overview of the system
4	
5	FIG. 1 shows a charging control system in which an edge controller 100 manages charging at a plurality of electric-vehicle connectors supplied by a common electrical branch. A branch conductor 102 supplies the plurality of connectors from a single point of protection. The allowable aggregate current of the branch conductor 102, referred to in this description as the branch limit, is lower than the sum of the ratings of the connectors that the branch conductor 102 supplies. The branch limit is a stored value that corresponds to the aggregate current the branch is permitted to carry, and may be derived from the rating of the protective device of the branch, from a site limit imposed by the supplying utility or by an energy management authority, or from both.
6	
7	The branch conductor 102 supplies a first connector station 110 and a second connector station 112. Two connector stations are shown for clarity of illustration. The system accommodates a larger plurality of connector stations, and the description of the first connector station 110 applies to each further connector station of the plurality. The branch conductor 102 also supplies a non-charging load 114, which represents lighting, building services, and other equipment that is connected to the same branch and that is not under the control of the edge controller 100.
8	
9	A branch current sensor 104 measures total current on the branch conductor 102 upstream of the contactors of the connector stations. Because the branch current sensor 104 is located upstream of those contactors, the current it measures includes both the current drawn by the connector stations and the current drawn by the non-charging load 114. The branch current sensor 104 may be a current transformer, a Rogowski coil, a Hall-effect sensor, a shunt with an isolated amplifier, or another transducer that reports the magnitude of alternating current on a conductor. Where the branch is polyphase, the branch current sensor 104 comprises a transducer for each phase conductor of the branch, and measured branch current is taken as the greatest of the per-phase magnitudes, so that the branch limit governs the most heavily loaded phase.
10	
11	The edge controller 100 communicates with the connector stations over an isolated local bus 106. 14	
15	The connector station
16	
17	FIG. 2 shows the first connector station 110 of FIG. 1 in greater detail. The first contactor 120 is connected in the power path between the branch conductor 102 and the first vehicle connector 126 and, when closed, permits current to flow from the branch conductor 102 to a vehicle coupled to the first vehicle connector 126. 18	
19	The first control-pilot interface 124 presents a control-pilot signal to the vehicle coupled to the first vehicle connector 126. The control-pilot signal advertises a maximum current, called here the assigned limit, that the vehicle is permitted to draw, and reports the state of the coupling, including whether a vehicle is connected and whether that vehicle is requesting energy. 20	
21	Each connector station of the plurality further has a local connector identifier. The local connector identifier is a stored value that distinguishes one connector of the plurality from another in the records, authorizations, and assignments held by the edge controller 100. The local connector identifier is a data value and does not appear as an inscription on the connector station in the drawings.
22	
23	The distinction between the first control-pilot interface 124 and the first connector current sensor 122 is used throughout this description. The first control-pilot interface 124 carries a command. The first connector current sensor 122 carries a measurement. The edge controller 100 does not treat the assigned limit sent through the first control-pilot interface 124 as evidence of the current that the connector is drawing. It obtains that evidence from the first connector current sensor 122.
24	
25	The edge controller
26	
27	FIG. 3 shows the edge controller 100 of FIG. 1 in greater detail. The edge controller 100 comprises a processing circuit 130 and a nonvolatile memory 132, and is coupled to the isolated local bus 106 and to the network interface 108. The processing circuit 130 may be a microcontroller, a microprocessor with associated volatile memory, a system on a chip, a programmable logic device, or a combination of such devices, and executes the allocation and protection processes described below. The nonvolatile memory 132 retains stored values across loss of supply, and may be flash memory, electrically erasable programmable read-only memory, ferroelectric memory, or another non-volatile storage device.
28	
29	The edge controller 100 further comprises a local fault indicator 134 and a service input 136. The local fault indicator 134 provides an indication at the equipment itself, independently of the network interface 108, and may be a lamp, an illuminated legend, a display element, or an audible annunciator. The service input 136 is an input by which an installer places the edge controller 100 in a commissioning mode, and may be a physical control on the equipment, a locally connected service terminal, or a maintenance port that requires physical access to the enclosure of the edge controller 100.
30	
31	For each active connector of the plurality, the edge controller 100 stores a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current, and an energy-deficit value. The charging authorization records that the session at that connector is permitted to draw energy. The requested current is the current that the session would take if capacity were unconstrained, and may be obtained from the vehicle by way of the control-pilot interface of that connector, from the rating of the connector, or from a stored session parameter. The minimum sustaining current is the smallest assigned limit at which the session at that connector is expected to remain charging rather than terminating and requiring a new start, and may be a value that is common to the plurality of connectors or a value stored for each connector individually. The energy-deficit value represents the extent to which the session at that connector has been served less than its requested current over the shared-capacity period. In some implementations the energy-deficit value is accumulated over successive allocation intervals from the difference between the requested current of the session and the current assigned to that session. In other implementations the energy-deficit value is accumulated from the difference between the requested current and the connector current measured by the connector current sensor of that connector, which additionally accounts for a vehicle that draws less than it was permitted to draw. In further implementations the energy-deficit value is derived from a stored energy target for the session and the energy delivered to that session so far. Any of these implementations gives a value that increases while a session is held below its request and decreases as the shortfall is made up, and the allocation process described below uses only that property of the value.
32	
33	Allocation at each allocation interval
34	
35	FIG. 4 shows the process carried out by the edge controller 100. The edge controller 100 repeats the allocation portion of the process at each allocation interval. 36	
37	At an available-charging-current determination step 200, the edge controller 100 subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch limit to obtain an available charging current. The measured non-charging branch load is obtained from the branch current sensor 104 and the connector current sensors: the edge controller 100 takes the difference between the measured branch current and the sum of the connector currents measured at the connector stations, so that the portion of the branch current drawn by the non-charging load 114 is determined by measurement rather than by assumption. The configurable safety reserve is a stored margin that is withheld from allocation, and accommodates the measurement tolerance of the sensors, the step size and settling behaviour of vehicles responding to a changed assigned limit, and any increase in the non-charging load 114 that occurs between allocation intervals. Because the non-charging portion of the branch load is measured at each allocation interval and subtracted at the determination step 200, the available charging current follows the varying load of the site, and capacity released by the non-charging load 114 becomes available to the connectors instead of being permanently withheld.
38	
39	At a minimum sustaining current assignment step 202, the edge controller 100 first assigns the minimum sustaining current to the sessions that can receive it. The edge controller 100 takes the active connectors in turn and assigns the minimum sustaining current of each to that connector for as long as the available charging current has not been exhausted. A session for which a remaining part of the available charging current at that allocation interval is less than its minimum sustaining current cannot receive the minimum sustaining current, and is assigned no current at that allocation interval rather than being assigned a value below its minimum sustaining current. Assigning a value below the minimum sustaining current would be worse than assigning nothing, because the session would be likely to terminate while still consuming allocated capacity, and would then require a new start. Where the available charging current is insufficient for every active session to receive its minimum sustaining current, the edge controller 100 selects the sessions to be sustained in order of energy deficit, so that the sessions that have been served least are sustained first.
40	
41	At a deficit-based distribution step 204, the edge controller 100 distributes the remaining portion of the available charging current, that is, the portion left after the assignments made at the minimum sustaining current assignment step 202, according to energy deficit. Sessions with a greater energy-deficit value receive a greater share of the remaining current than sessions with a smaller energy-deficit value. The distribution may be made in proportion to the energy-deficit values of the sessions, or by allocating to the session with the greatest energy-deficit value until its energy-deficit value falls to that of the next session and then allocating to those sessions together, or by another rule that orders the shares by energy deficit. No session is assigned more than its requested current, and any current that remains after every session has reached its requested current is left unassigned and is therefore added to the margin held on the branch. Distributing by energy deficit rather than by instantaneous request corrects, rather than perpetuates, the inequality that arises when one session begins while the branch is heavily loaded and another begins while it is lightly loaded.

43	At a limit transmission and connector current verification step 206, the edge controller 100 sends each assigned limit through the control-pilot interface of the corresponding connector, and then verifies the resulting connector current with the connector current sensor of that connector. Where the measured connector current exceeds the assigned limit of that connector, the connector is not honouring the command it has been given, and the edge controller 100 records the deviation for that connector and treats the measured connector current, rather than the assigned limit, as the load that the connector places on the branch at the next allocation interval. The allocation is in this way closed loop at each connector: a connector that draws less than it has been permitted does not cause capacity to be withheld from the others, and a connector that draws more than it has been permitted does not cause the branch to be overcommitted at the next interval.
44	
45	The branch current sensor as an independent safety input
46	
47	The branch current sensor 104 is an independent safety input. 48	
49	At a pilot reduction step 208, the edge controller 100 compares the measured branch current from the branch current sensor 104 with the branch limit. The reduced pilot command is the first stage of the response, because reducing current through the control pilot lets a vehicle taper its draw and lets the session continue, which is preferable to interrupting the power path.
50	
51	At an ordered contactor shedding step 210, the edge controller 100 determines whether the measured branch current remains above the branch limit after the reduced pilot command and after the verification interval has elapsed. The verification interval is long enough for a vehicle that honours the reduced pilot command to have acted on it. If the measured branch current has fallen below the branch limit within the verification interval, the reduced pilot command has been effective and the edge controller 100 returns to the allocation interval process. If the measured branch current remains above the branch limit at the end of the verification interval, the pilot signalling has not produced the required reduction, and the edge controller 100 opens the connector contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch limit.
52	
53	The shedding order is stored in the nonvolatile memory 132 and defines the sequence in which the contactors of the plurality of connector stations are opened. 54	
55	The staged sequence of a reduced pilot command, a verification interval, and then ordered interruption of the power path addresses the technical problem set out in the background. Allocation that works only from commanded values cannot detect that condition at all. A report of a connected vehicle from the control-pilot interface establishes that there is a session to restore, so that the power path is not energized to a coupling from which the vehicle has been removed. The randomized recovery delay is drawn afresh for each contactor from a configured range, so that two contactors of the plurality do not become synchronized across successive events.
62	
63	On reclosing, the edge controller 100 resumes the allocation interval process, and the reclosed session takes part in the assignments made at the minimum sustaining current assignment step 202 and the deficit-based distribution step 204 in the ordinary way.

70	
71	Operation during a network outage
72	
73	The edge controller 100 can receive remote schedules and authorizations through the network interface 108. A remote schedule may set the branch limit for a period of the day, and a remote authorization may permit a session at a given connector.

The last accepted branch limit is the most recent branch limit that the edge controller 100 has accepted from the remote management system.
76	
77	During a network outage the edge controller 100 continues already authorized sessions subject to the last accepted branch limit and the independent branch-current safety process described above. A newly connected vehicle at a connector that the token does not authorize, or a newly connected vehicle at any connector after the token has expired, is not started until communication returns and a fresh authorization is obtained.
78	
79	Meter records are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence held in the nonvolatile memory 132. Each record is appended to the sequence together with a value computed over that record and over the preceding entry of the sequence, so that removal, reordering, or alteration of an entry is detectable from the sequence itself. The records accumulated during the outage are uploaded when communication returns, and the sequence values are uploaded with them, so that the remote management system can confirm that the uploaded run is complete and unaltered.

The transition is a low-energy one, sufficient to produce a distinguishable response at the connector current sensor of the connector that is actually being driven, and the transitions are commanded one at a time so that the responding channel is unambiguous.
86	
87	The association between a connector identifier and a physical contactor is stored in the nonvolatile memory 132 only after the sensed channel agrees with the commanded connector. The mapping is thus established by measurement on the same sensors that the allocation process later relies upon, so a wiring-map error is found at commissioning instead of silently misdirecting current limits for the life of the installation.

90	
91	The allocation process, the branch protection process, the offline authorization behaviour, the welded-contactor isolation, and the installation mapping are described together because they share the sensors and the isolated local bus 106 of a single edge controller 100. An embodiment may carry out the allocation and branch protection processes without the offline authorization behaviour, without the tamper-evident record sequence, or without the commissioning mode, and an embodiment may include any combination of those additional features.
92	
93	The processes described above may be embodied as instructions stored on a non-transitory computer-readable medium and executed by the processing circuit 130. The values described as stored, including the branch limit, the configurable safety reserve, the minimum sustaining current, the shedding order, the leakage threshold, the range of the randomized recovery delay, the length of the allocation interval, and the length of the verification interval, may be configured at installation, may be set through the network interface 108, or may be held as defaults in the nonvolatile memory 132.
94	
95	The terms first and second are used to distinguish one connector station of the plurality from another and do not imply an order of importance or of operation. The system is not limited to two connector stations, and the description of the first connector station 110 applies to each connector station of the plurality. The embodiments described here are illustrative, and a person skilled in the art will recognize that elements described in connection with one embodiment may be combined with elements described in connection with another. The scope of the invention is defined by the claims that follow.

If the measured branch current remains above the branch limit at the end of the verification interval, the pilot signalling has not produced the required reduction, and the edge controller 100 opens the connector contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch limit.

The shedding order is stored in the nonvolatile memory 132 and defines the sequence in which the contactors of the plurality of connector stations are opened. The shedding order may be configured at installation, may be arranged so that the most recently started session is opened first, or may be arranged so that the session with the smallest energy-deficit value is opened first, so that the session that has already been served most is the one that gives up its power path. Opening the contactors one at a time, with the measured branch current re-evaluated between openings, removes only as much load as the measurement shows to be necessary: as soon as the measured branch current is below the branch limit, no further contactor is opened, and the remaining sessions continue.

The staged sequence of a reduced pilot command, a verification interval, and then ordered interruption of the power path addresses the technical problem set out in the background. A control-pilot command is advisory, and a vehicle that ignores it, responds too slowly, or responds only in coarse steps leaves the branch loaded above its limit. Allocation that works only from commanded values cannot detect that condition at all. By taking the measured branch current from a sensor that is upstream of every connector contactor, and by treating the persistence of an over-limit measurement through a verification interval as the trigger for opening the power path, the edge controller 100 bounds the branch current with an action that is entirely within its own control, while still giving the cooperative case the opportunity to resolve without interrupting any session.

Recovery after shedding

At a reclose permissive step 212, the edge controller 100 governs the reclosing of a contactor that has been opened by the ordered contactor shedding step 210. The edge controller 100 does not reclose such a contactor until three conditions are satisfied together: the connector current sensor of that connector reports zero current, the control-pilot interface of that connector reports a connected vehicle, and a randomized recovery delay has expired.

Each condition addresses a distinct hazard. A report of zero current from the connector current sensor establishes that the power path is in fact open, so that a reclose command is not issued onto a path that is still carrying current. A report of a connected vehicle from the control-pilot interface establishes that there is a session to restore, so that the power path is not energized to a coupling from which the vehicle has been removed. The randomized recovery delay separates in time the reclosing of the contactors that were shed together, and separates the recovery of the equipment from the recovery of other equipment responding to the same site event, so that the loads do not return in unison and reproduce the overload that the shedding sequence has just relieved. The randomized recovery delay is drawn afresh for each contactor from a configured range, so that two contactors of the plurality do not become synchronized across successive events.

On reclosing, the edge controller 100 resumes the allocation interval process, and the reclosed session takes part in the assignments made at the minimum sustaining current assignment step 202 and the deficit-based distribution step 204 in the ordinary way.

Welded-contactor isolation

At a welded-contactor isolation step 214, the edge controller 100 records a welded-contactor condition for a connector when the connector current measured by the connector current sensor of that connector remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector. The leakage threshold is a stored current magnitude above zero, chosen to be above the residual measurement that the connector current sensor reports on an open path and below any current that would represent load, so that sensor noise and standing offsets are not mistaken for a welded contact.

When the welded-contactor condition has been recorded, the edge controller 100 inhibits the other contactors on the same branch and operates the local fault indicator 134. The other contactors are inhibited because a welded contactor consumes branch capacity that neither the allocation process nor the shedding sequence can recover: the shedding sequence believes that opening that contactor has released the current of that connector, and any further allocation made on that belief would overcommit the branch. Inhibiting the other contactors removes the controllable load from the branch and leaves only the current of the welded connector, which is the safe state available to the edge controller 100 with the means at its disposal. The local fault indicator 134 is operated at the equipment because the condition requires physical service and because it must be annunciated whether or not the network interface 108 is available.

Operation during a network outage

The edge controller 100 can receive remote schedules and authorizations through the network interface 108. A remote schedule may set the branch limit for a period of the day, and a remote authorization may permit a session at a given connector.

The edge controller 100 stores a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit in the nonvolatile memory 132. The signed local authorization token is issued by the remote management system, carries a cryptographic signature that the edge controller 100 verifies against a stored key, identifies the connectors it authorizes by their local connector identifiers, and carries an expiry. The last accepted branch limit is the most recent branch limit that the edge controller 100 has accepted from the remote management system.

During a network outage the edge controller 100 continues already authorized sessions subject to the last accepted branch limit and the independent branch-current safety process described above. Charging therefore continues through the outage, and continues within a limit that a responsible authority has set, rather than within a limit chosen locally because no other limit is available. The edge controller 100 does not start a newly connected session unless the signed local authorization token authorizes that connector and has not expired. A newly connected vehicle at a connector that the token does not authorize, or a newly connected vehicle at any connector after the token has expired, is not started until communication returns and a fresh authorization is obtained.

Meter records are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence held in the nonvolatile memory 132. Each record is appended to the sequence together with a value computed over that record and over the preceding entry of the sequence, so that removal, reordering, or alteration of an entry is detectable from the sequence itself. The records accumulated during the outage are uploaded when communication returns, and the sequence values are uploaded with them, so that the remote management system can confirm that the uploaded run is complete and unaltered.

Installation mapping through the service input

A multi-connector installation is wired by hand, and the identifier a connector is given in configuration must correspond to the physical contactor and the physical current sensor channel that serve that connector. A transposition assigns a current limit intended for one connector to another. Every component continues to function, every sensor continues to report, and the allocation nevertheless governs the wrong power path.

The service input 136 permits an installer to associate connector identifiers with physical contactors. With the edge controller 100 in the commissioning mode entered through the service input 136, the edge controller 100 commands one low-energy pilot transition at a time, that is, it drives a pilot transition at a single connector, and confirms the corresponding connector current sensor by observing which sensed channel responds to that transition. The transition is a low-energy one, sufficient to produce a distinguishable response at the connector current sensor of the connector that is actually being driven, and the transitions are commanded one at a time so that the responding channel is unambiguous.

The association between a connector identifier and a physical contactor is stored in the nonvolatile memory 132 only after the sensed channel agrees with the commanded connector. If the responding channel is not the channel expected for the commanded connector, or if no channel responds, no association is stored for that connector. The mapping is thus established by measurement on the same sensors that the allocation process later relies upon, so a wiring-map error is found at commissioning instead of silently misdirecting current limits for the life of the installation.

General considerations

The allocation process, the branch protection process, the offline authorization behaviour, the welded-contactor isolation, and the installation mapping are described together because they share the sensors and the isolated local bus 106 of a single edge controller 100. They are nevertheless separable. An embodiment may carry out the allocation and branch protection processes without the offline authorization behaviour, without the tamper-evident record sequence, or without the commissioning mode, and an embodiment may include any combination of those additional features.

The processes described above may be embodied as instructions stored on a non-transitory computer-readable medium and executed by the processing circuit 130. The values described as stored, including the branch limit, the configurable safety reserve, the minimum sustaining current, the shedding order, the leakage threshold, the range of the randomized recovery delay, the length of the allocation interval, and the length of the verification interval, may be configured at installation, may be set through the network interface 108, or may be held as defaults in the nonvolatile memory 132.

The terms first and second are used to distinguish one connector station of the plurality from another and do not imply an order of importance or of operation. The system is not limited to two connector stations, and the description of the first connector station 110 applies to each connector station of the plurality. The embodiments described here are illustrative, and a person skilled in the art will recognize that elements described in connection with one embodiment may be combined with elements described in connection with another. input.summary:
Reviewed disclosure.md, conversation.md (single USER passage, identical to the disclosure), brief.md, all ten draft sections, numerals.md, and the four figure briefs. The prior art given may be incomplete; no prior-art references are cited in the Background, so no citation tracing was required here. No section lines or sectional views exist in any figure brief, so the v9 section-line designation check is vacuous — nothing to report there. No drafting notes, placeholders, open questions, or unresolved alternatives remain in the draft files.

The core spine traces cleanly: the branch limit below the sum of connector ratings, per-connector contactor / connector current sensor / control-pilot interface / local connector identifier, the upstream branch current sensor, the isolated local bus to the connector interfaces and contactors, the four stored per-session values, the subtract-non-charging-load-and-safety-reserve allocation, minimum-sustaining-then-deficit distribution, pilot transmission with connector-current verification, the reduced-pilot-command / verification-interval / ordered-shedding staging, the three-condition reclose permissive, welded-contactor recording with inhibition of the other contactors and a local fault indicator, offline token and last-accepted-branch-limit behaviour, tamper-evident meter records, and service-input commissioning mapping.

Twenty findings fall outside that spine. The most serious is a three-way conflict about how the branch current sensor reaches the controller: claims 1 and 20 recite the controller "coupled ... to the branch current sensor over the isolated local bus," the FIG. 1 brief draws a dedicated separate line from sensor 104 to the top edge of controller 100 with "No block ... drawn on this line," the FIG. 3 brief shows no branch-sensor port at all, and the disclosure places only "the connector interfaces and contactors" on that bus. That is simultaneously an unsupported claim limitation and an internal inconsistency.

A second group is unsupported technical mechanism recited in dependent claims: the non-charging load derived as branch current minus the sum of connector currents (claims 2, 16 and step 200); per-contactor randomized delays drawn from a configured range (claim 4); polyphase per-phase transducers with a greatest-magnitude rule (claim 14); the compare-and-substitute verification rule (claim 13); assigning zero rather than a sub-minimum current (claim 11); deficit-ordered selection of which sessions are sustained (claim 12); and the chained value computed over each meter record and the preceding entry (claim 9). The disclosure states each corresponding concept only at the level of "measured non-charging branch load," "a randomized recovery delay," "verifies the resulting connector current," "sessions that can receive it," and "a tamper-evident local sequence." None of the mechanisms above appears in any USER passage.

A third group is optional-embodiment prose in the detailed description that the inventor never supplied: three alternative constructions of the energy-deficit value; three alternative shedding-order rules; two alternative deficit-distribution algorithms; the requested-current sources; the per-connector-or-common minimum sustaining current; branch-limit derivation from a protective-device rating or utility/energy-management site limit; the remote schedule setting the branch limit "for a period of the day"; the no-session-above-its-request / surplus-left-unassigned rule; the galvanic-isolation function and three bus implementations; and the hardware menus for the branch current sensor, network interface, processing circuit, nonvolatile memory, local fault indicator, and service input. The identification of non-charging load 114 as "lighting, building services, and other equipment" is drawn from the Background's prior-art framing, not from any inventor passage. The non-transitory computer-readable medium class (claim 20, summary, description) likewise has no disclosure antecedent.

Remaining findings are internal: network interface 108 sits outside edge controller 100 in FIG. 1 but inside its enclosure in FIG. 3 while the text says the controller is "coupled to" it; claim 7 restates the safety process as direct shedding on an over-limit measurement, dropping the staged pilot reduction that claim 1 makes mandatory; the FIG. 2 series order placing sensor 122 downstream of contactor 120 is a topology choice with no source; and description line 21's remark that the identifier "does not appear as an inscription ... in the drawings" is a renderer-justification note that should not remain in the application text. The title also adds subject matter beyond the brief's working title.

Every finding below quotes the candidate wording, quotes or names the nearest source passage showing the gap, and gives a filing-clean fix.

findings.title: Claims 1 and 20 put the branch current sensor on the isolated local bus; the disclosure, the description, and FIG. 1 do not
findings.where: draft/09-claims.md claim 1 and claim 20 preamble; figures/FIG-1.md; figures/FIG-3.md; draft/08-detailed-description.md paras. at lines 9, 11
findings.detail: Claim 1 recites "a controller coupled to the plurality of connector stations and to the branch current sensor over the isolated local bus", and claim 20 recites "a controller coupled over an isolated local bus to a plurality of connector stations ... and to a branch current sensor". The inventor placed only the connector interfaces and contactors on that bus. The description never states how sensor 104 reaches controller 100, and the FIG. 1 brief affirmatively draws a dedicated, separate connection outside the bus. FIG. 3 shows no branch-sensor port at all. This is both an untraced claim limitation and a three-way internal inconsistency between claims, description, and drawings.
findings.evidence: Candidate (claim 1): "a controller coupled to the plurality of connector stations and to the branch current sensor over the isolated local bus". Candidate (FIG-1.md): "A separate line runs from the branch current sensor 104 downward and to the left, clear of the three rectangles, to the top edge of the edge controller 100. No block is drawn on this line." Candidate (08, line 11): "The isolated local bus 106 carries assigned current limits and contactor commands from the edge controller 100 to the connector stations, and carries connector current measurements and control-pilot status from the connector stations to the edge controller 100." Nearest source (disclosure.md para. 1): "A branch current sensor measures total current upstream of the connector contactors. A controller communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus." No affirmative passage places the branch current sensor on the isolated local bus.
findings.fix: In claim 1 replace "a controller coupled to the plurality of connector stations and to the branch current sensor over the isolated local bus" with "a controller coupled to the plurality of connector stations over the isolated local bus and coupled to the branch current sensor". In claim 20 replace "a controller coupled over an isolated local bus to a plurality of connector stations supplied by a common electrical branch and to a branch current sensor arranged to measure" with "a controller coupled over an isolated local bus to a plurality of connector stations supplied by a common electrical branch and coupled to a branch current sensor arranged to measure".

findings.title: Non-charging branch load computed as branch current minus the sum of connector currents is not disclosed
findings.where: draft/09-claims.md claims 2 and 16; draft/08-detailed-description.md para. at line 37
findings.detail: The disclosure states only that the controller "subtracts measured non-charging branch load" from the branch limit. It never specifies how that quantity is obtained. The candidate recites a specific arithmetic derivation from two sensor sets, which is added technical substance in an independent-supporting dependent claim and in the description of step 200.
findings.evidence: Candidate (claim 2): "wherein the controller is configured to obtain the measured non-charging branch load as a difference between the measured branch current and a sum of the connector currents measured by the connector current sensors of the plurality of connector stations." Candidate (08, line 37): "the edge controller 100 takes the difference between the measured branch current and the sum of the connector currents measured at the connector stations". Nearest source (disclosure.md para. 2): "the controller subtracts measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch limit to obtain an available charging current." No affirmative passage discloses the difference computation.
findings.fix: Delete claim 2 and claim 16 and renumber the remaining claims and their dependencies accordingly. In draft/08-detailed-description.md line 37, delete "The measured non-charging branch load is obtained from the branch current sensor 104 and the connector current sensors: the edge controller 100 takes the difference between the measured branch current and the sum of the connector currents measured at the connector stations, so that the portion of the branch current drawn by the non-charging load 114 is determined by measurement rather than by assumption." and replace it with "The measured non-charging branch load is the measured portion of the branch current that is drawn by the non-charging load 114."

findings.title: Polyphase branch with a per-phase transducer and greatest-magnitude rule is not disclosed
findings.where: draft/09-claims.md claim 14; draft/08-detailed-description.md para. at line 9
findings.detail: Claim 14 and the description recite a polyphase embodiment, a transducer per phase conductor, and a rule taking the greatest per-phase magnitude as the measured branch current. The disclosure describes a single branch current sensor and says nothing about phases, per-phase transducers, or a maximum-selection rule.
findings.evidence: Candidate (claim 14): "wherein the electrical branch is polyphase, the branch current sensor comprises a transducer for each phase conductor of the electrical branch, and the controller is configured to take as the measured branch current the greatest of the per-phase current magnitudes reported by the transducers." structured_output.summary:
Reviewed disclosure.md, conversation.md (single USER passage, identical to the disclosure), brief.md, all ten draft sections, numerals.md, and the four figure briefs. The prior art given may be incomplete; no prior-art references are cited in the Background, so no citation tracing was required here. No section lines or sectional views exist in any figure brief, so the v9 section-line designation check is vacuous — nothing to report there. No drafting notes, placeholders, open questions, or unresolved alternatives remain in the draft files.

The core spine traces cleanly: the branch limit below the sum of connector ratings, per-connector contactor / connector current sensor / control-pilot interface / local connector identifier, the upstream branch current sensor, the isolated local bus to the connector interfaces and contactors, the four stored per-session values, the subtract-non-charging-load-and-safety-reserve allocation, minimum-sustaining-then-deficit distribution, pilot transmission with connector-current verification, the reduced-pilot-command / verification-interval / ordered-shedding staging, the three-condition reclose permissive, welded-contactor recording with inhibition of the other contactors and a local fault indicator, offline token and last-accepted-branch-limit behaviour, tamper-evident meter records, and service-input commissioning mapping.

Twenty findings fall outside that spine. The most serious is a three-way conflict about how the branch current sensor reaches the controller: claims 1 and 20 recite the controller "coupled ... to the branch current sensor over the isolated local bus," the FIG. 1 brief draws a dedicated separate line from sensor 104 to the top edge of controller 100 with "No block ... drawn on this line," the FIG. 3 brief shows no branch-sensor port at all, and the disclosure places only "the connector interfaces and contactors" on that bus. That is simultaneously an unsupported claim limitation and an internal inconsistency.

A second group is unsupported technical mechanism recited in dependent claims: the non-charging load derived as branch current minus the sum of connector currents (claims 2, 16 and step 200); per-contactor randomized delays drawn from a configured range (claim 4); polyphase per-phase transducers with a greatest-magnitude rule (claim 14); the compare-and-substitute verification rule (claim 13); assigning zero rather than a sub-minimum current (claim 11); deficit-ordered selection of which sessions are sustained (claim 12); and the chained value computed over each meter record and the preceding entry (claim 9). The disclosure states each corresponding concept only at the level of "measured non-charging branch load," "a randomized recovery delay," "verifies the resulting connector current," "sessions that can receive it," and "a tamper-evident local sequence." None of the mechanisms above appears in any USER passage.

A third group is optional-embodiment prose in the detailed description that the inventor never supplied: three alternative constructions of the energy-deficit value; three alternative shedding-order rules; two alternative deficit-distribution algorithms; the requested-current sources; the per-connector-or-common minimum sustaining current; branch-limit derivation from a protective-device rating or utility/energy-management site limit; the remote schedule setting the branch limit "for a period of the day"; the no-session-above-its-request / surplus-left-unassigned rule; the galvanic-isolation function and three bus implementations; and the hardware menus for the branch current sensor, network interface, processing circuit, nonvolatile memory, local fault indicator, and service input. The identification of non-charging load 114 as "lighting, building services, and other equipment" is drawn from the Background's prior-art framing, not from any inventor passage. The non-transitory computer-readable medium class (claim 20, summary, description) likewise has no disclosure antecedent.

Remaining findings are internal: network interface 108 sits outside edge controller 100 in FIG. 1 but inside its enclosure in FIG. 3 while the text says the controller is "coupled to" it; claim 7 restates the safety process as direct shedding on an over-limit measurement, dropping the staged pilot reduction that claim 1 makes mandatory; the FIG. 2 series order placing sensor 122 downstream of contactor 120 is a topology choice with no source; and description line 21's remark that the identifier "does not appear as an inscription ... in the drawings" is a renderer-justification note that should not remain in the application text. The title also adds subject matter beyond the brief's working title.

findings.where: draft/09-claims.md claim 11 (and claim 12's dependency); draft/08-detailed-description.md para. at line 39
findings.detail: The disclosure says the minimum sustaining current is assigned "to sessions that can receive it", which does not state what a session that cannot receive it is assigned. Under the disclosed two-stage process such a session could still receive a share at the deficit-distribution stage. The candidate affirmatively forecloses that by assigning zero, which is added allocation substance and also narrows the disclosed process.
findings.evidence: Candidate (claim 11): "the controller is configured to assign no current at the allocation interval to a session of an active connector for which a remaining part of the available charging current at that allocation interval is less than the minimum sustaining current of that active connector, rather than to assign to that session a current below its minimum sustaining current." Candidate (08, line 39): "and is assigned no current at that allocation interval rather than being assigned a value below its minimum sustaining current." Nearest source (disclosure.md para. 2): "It first assigns the minimum sustaining current to sessions that can receive it, then distributes remaining current according to energy deficit." No affirmative passage states the zero-assignment rule.
findings.fix: Delete claim 11 and renumber the remaining claims (claim 12 is separately deleted above). In draft/08-detailed-description.md line 39, delete ", and is assigned no current at that allocation interval rather than being assigned a value below its minimum sustaining current" and delete the following sentence "Assigning a value below the minimum sustaining current would be worse than assigning nothing, because the session would be likely to terminate while still consuming allocated capacity, and would then require a new start."

findings.title: Non-transitory computer-readable medium embodiment has no disclosure antecedent
findings.where: draft/09-claims.md claim 20; draft/06-summary.md para. at line 17; draft/08-detailed-description.md para. at line 93
findings.detail: The disclosure describes a controller and processes but never mentions software, stored instructions, a processing circuit executing instructions, or a computer-readable medium. Claim 20 recites a distinct article of manufacture built on structure that no USER passage supplies.
findings.evidence: Candidate (claim 20): "A non-transitory computer-readable medium storing instructions that, when executed by a processing circuit of a controller ... cause the controller to:". Candidate (06, line 17): "and a non-transitory computer-readable medium storing instructions that carry out the method." Candidate (08, line 93): "The processes described above may be embodied as instructions stored on a non-transitory computer-readable medium and executed by the processing circuit 130." Nearest source (disclosure.md para. 1): "A controller communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus." No affirmative passage discloses stored instructions or a medium.
findings.fix: Delete claim 20 and, in draft/06-summary.md line 17, replace the sentence with "Embodiments include a charging control system and a method of controlling charging at a plurality of electric-vehicle connectors supplied by a common electrical branch." In draft/08-detailed-description.md line 93, delete the sentence "The processes described above may be embodied as instructions stored on a non-transitory computer-readable medium and executed by the processing circuit 130."

findings.title: Network interface 108 is outside the edge controller in FIG. 1 but inside its enclosure in FIG. 3, and the text says the controller is coupled to it
findings.where: figures/FIG-1.md geometry bullet 14; figures/FIG-3.md geometry bullet 10; draft/08-detailed-description.md paras. at lines 13 and 27
findings.detail: The same numbered part is given two different structural relationships to the edge controller across the two figures, and the description's language ("is coupled to ... the network interface 108") matches the FIG. 1 arrangement while contradicting the FIG. 3 arrangement. A numbered part must mean one thing across the views.
findings.evidence: Candidate (FIG-1.md): "A small plain rectangle stands immediately to the left of the edge controller 100 and is joined to the left side of the edge controller 100 by a short horizontal line. This rectangle is the network interface 108." Candidate (FIG-3.md): "A plain rectangle stands to the left of the processing circuit 130, within the enclosing rectangle, joined by a horizontal line to the left side of the processing circuit 130. This left rectangle is the network interface 108". Candidate (08, line 27): "The edge controller 100 comprises a processing circuit 130 and a nonvolatile memory 132, and is coupled to the isolated local bus 106 and to the network interface 108."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-3.md, change the bullet to place the network interface outside the enclosing rectangle, consistent with FIG. 1: "A plain rectangle stands to the left of the enclosing rectangle, outside it, joined by a horizontal line that passes through the left side of the enclosing rectangle to the left side of the processing circuit 130. This rectangle is the network interface 108, shown schematically. A short line extends from the left side of the network interface 108 and terminates inside the drawing area."

findings.title: Claim 7 describes the offline safety process as direct shedding, dropping the staged pilot reduction that claim 1 makes mandatory
findings.where: draft/09-claims.md claim 7
findings.detail: Claim 1 requires that shedding occur only after a reduced pilot command has been sent and a verification interval has elapsed. Claim 7, which depends on claim 1, recites shedding conditioned only on the measured branch current remaining above the last accepted branch limit, describing a different, unstaged trigger. That conflicts with claim 1 and with the description, which states that the staged sequence is what governs, and it also departs from the inventor's phrase "the independent branch-current safety process".
findings.evidence: Candidate (claim 7): "to continue already authorized sessions subject to the last accepted branch limit and subject to opening the contactors in the stored shedding order when the measured branch current remains above the last accepted branch limit." Candidate (claim 1): "when the measured branch current remains above the branch limit after the reduced pilot command has been sent and a verification interval has elapsed, to open the contactors ... one at a time in a stored shedding order". Source (disclosure.md para. 4): "it continues already authorized sessions subject to the last accepted branch limit and the independent branch-current safety process."
findings.fix: In claim 7, replace "and subject to opening the contactors in the stored shedding order when the measured branch current remains above the last accepted branch limit" with "and subject to the reduced pilot command and the opening of the contactors in the stored shedding order recited in claim 1, applied with the last accepted branch limit as the branch limit".

findings.title: Description contains a drawing-convention note that should not remain in the application text
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md para. at line 21 (last sentence)
findings.detail: The sentence exists only to explain why the renderer omitted an inscription from the drawings. It is a drafting note about the figures rather than a description of the invention, and drawing conventions must stay confined to the figure briefs.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The local connector identifier is a data value and does not appear as an inscription on the connector station in the drawings." The preceding sentence already states the substance the inventor disclosed: "The local connector identifier is a stored value that distinguishes one connector of the plurality from another".
findings.fix: In draft/08-detailed-description.md line 21, delete the sentence "The local connector identifier is a data value and does not appear as an inscription on the connector station in the drawings."

findings.title: FIG. 2 fixes the connector current sensor downstream of the contactor, a topology the disclosure does not specify
findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md geometry bullets 9-10
findings.detail: The disclosure places the branch sensor upstream of the connector contactors but says nothing about the relative order of the contactor and the connector current sensor within a connector's power path. The brief asserts a specific series order, which is a technical relationship rather than a shape convention.
findings.evidence: Candidate (FIG-2.md): "A small open rectangle straddles the power path near the left of the enclosing rectangle ... This rectangle is the first contactor 120" followed by "A second small open rectangle straddles the same power path to the right of the first contactor 120 ... This rectangle is the first connector current sensor 122". Nearest source (disclosure.md para. 1): "Each connector has a controllable contactor, a connector current sensor, a control-pilot interface, and a local connector identifier." No affirmative passage orders the two in the power path.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-2.md, add to the numeral-endpoint note the sentence "The order in which the first contactor 120 and the first connector current sensor 122 appear along the power path is a drawing convention only; both are in series in the same power path." and leave the geometry unchanged. Do not add any corresponding statement to the application text.
